summary: Greedy decoding isolated on contrastive-RAG best base
hypothesis: Swapping the single generation call from stochastic sampling to greedy (deterministic) decoding on the best contrastive-RAG base (exp011) should reduce noise and improve consistency, because every prior ~0.32 result was a single noisy draw and the deterministic mode might surface more task-specific unknowns.
technique: The exp011 contrastive-RAG topology was held completely fixed; only the decoding mode was changed to greedy (temperature 0, deterministic) on the single on-device generation call, isolating the decoding lever as a directly falsifiable test.
result: Scored 0.273 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), a regression of −0.050 vs exp011's best of 0.323 and −0.034 vs the 0.307 baseline; coverage pinned at 3 with the same recurring generic catch-alls verbatim, and nonRedundancy stayed at 3 with fresh overlaps — confirming that the model's modal output IS the generic one and that the decoding lever cannot move coverage. Discarded.
